claims.text: Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 is initially in a high-temperature BCC phase.
Phase stability in this alloy is governed by competition between a thermodynamic driving force for phase separation and kinetic constraints.
Aluminum-induced local ordering strengthens the thermodynamic driving force for phase separation.
High interfacial-energy barriers slow atomic diffusion.
The kinetic constraints cause metastable retention of the BCC phase.
Sufficient thermal energy permits transformation of the retained BCC phase.
Interfacial-energy barriers and aluminum-influenced local ordering modulate grain-boundary mobility.
Aluminum simultaneously increases interfacial-energy barriers that restrict atomic mobility.
Transformation from BCC to secondary phases proceeds only when thermal energy overcomes the proposed kinetic constraints.
Isothermal annealing will produce an earlier onset of secondary phases than fast quenching.
Isothermal annealing will produce larger quantities of secondary phases than fast quenching.
Microstructural modifications that reduce interfacial-energy barriers will accelerate transformation relative to untreated samples.
Fast quenching retains the high-temperature BCC structure by suppressing diffusion.
Kinetic barriers dominate phase behavior in Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 at approximately 650–800°C.
Significant compositional or microstructural inhomogeneity may invalidate the proposed mechanism.
